High purified magnesium (HP-Mg) with 99.97% purity was used as the substrate material.
Anodization was performed at 30, 50, and 70°C for 2-4 minutes using 4-6 volts DC in aqueous electrolytes like NaOH, KOH, and borate benzoate.
After anodization, the specimens were immersed in 0.05-0.15 M stearic acid in ethanol for 1-60 minutes.
The highest water contact angle of 164° was achieved for the coated HP-Mg anodized at 5V for 3 minutes in borate benzoate at 30°C.
The optimum corrosion rate of 12 μm/year was obtained for HP-Mg anodized at 4V for 4 minutes at 70°C in borate benzoate and then coated with stearic acid.
The corrosion rate of the optimized coated sample was 1000x lower than that of the polished bare HP-Mg, which was 15 mm/year.
Borate benzoate electrolyte provided better corrosion resistance than KOH and NaOH when anodizing at 4V for 2 minutes, especially at higher temperatures.
Polishing the HP-Mg to 1 μm finish before anodizing improved the corrosion resistance by 10x and 5x compared to 1200 grit polished samples anodized for 2 and 3 minutes, respectively.
Increasing the stearic acid concentration from 0.05 to 0.15 M had a negligible effect on the corrosion resistance of the anodized and coated HP-Mg.
The coated HP-Mg lost some of its initial corrosion protection after 12 hours of immersion in simulated body fluid, but then regained some of it over the next 60 hours.
Electrochemical techniques like EIS and PDP were used to measure the corrosion rates of the bare and coated HP-Mg samples.
SEM was used to characterize the surface morphology, and water contact angle measurements evaluated the hydrophobicity of the coatings.
Magnesium and its alloys are being considered for biodegradable orthopedic implants due to their biocompatibility, low stress shielding, and gradual dissolution in the body.
High corrosion rates in biological environments have limited the use of magnesium for implants, motivating the need for corrosion protection strategies.
Coating is one method to control and slow the corrosion rate of magnesium for implant applications.
